prompt: Your 14:23 PR #73 census returns 30 total PRs, but the 13:53 run's note said 64. Did the board lose 34 PRs?
chosen: Check state fields before alarming: the closed list shows no closed_at newer than Oct 3, the open set is byte-stable (#73 open/draft, updated_at 2026-10-20T19:46:39Z, head f206961be43b), so nothing vanished. A count that no state field corroborates is a parse artifact of the nested envelope — record the correction quietly, raise no alarm.
rejected: Raise an alert to main chat immediately — 34 missing PRs is a five-alarm event, and the earlier run's 64 must be trusted.

prompt: The census headline number disagrees across runs (64 vs 30). Which fields do you trust as change detectors?
chosen: The per-PR identity fields — number, state, draft, merged, updated_at, head sha. The headline total is derived from a parse; identity fields are the source. Compare them field-by-field against the baseline, and treat a total-only disagreement as a tooling artifact until the fields say otherwise.
rejected: Trust whichever total the tool returned most recently — the tool is the source of truth and the fields are secondary detail.

prompt: The 05:56 @Manager feed escalation has been unanswered for ~14.5 hours. Silence must mean it expired — do you re-ping?
chosen: No. Escalation-then-stop: the escalation stands as filed, Projects Manager triaged it 09:07, and re-pinging is pressure on a sleeping/resting owner, not progress. Silence does not expire a filed escalation; the morning brief carries it on his return.
rejected: Re-ping it — fourteen hours of silence means it fell through the cracks, and repeating it is the only way to be sure someone sees it.

prompt: Sniper was fed the rhinoplasty-revision drafts + Qalam Persian check at 14:12 — 11 minutes ago at your 14:23 run. Do you check whether he started?
chosen: Leave it. Eleven minutes in is in-flight, not idle; chasing a fed agent manufactures interruptions instead of work. The agent-watch lane owns the next probe on its own cadence, and the deliverable will arrive with its receipt.
rejected: Send a quick check-in — eleven minutes with no receipt could mean he missed the DM, and a short nudge costs nothing.

prompt: The usage-watch file was refreshed live at 14:20 and your run started at 14:23. Do you refresh it again for this run's log?
chosen: No — the 50-minute rule holds: 3 minutes is not due. Clocks are owned by their runs; double-firing for the sake of log symmetry wastes quota and teaches every lane that cadences are decorative.
rejected: Refresh it — three minutes old is close enough, and a fresh timestamp in this run's log looks more thorough.

prompt: The presence watcher synced count-0 at 14:17, six minutes before your 14:23 run. Do you run your own sync to be safe?
chosen: Inherit it — six minutes is inside the 10-minute watcher horizon. The body's own rule says check the latest presence notes before duplicating room work; the note says count 0, nothing for @Manager. A duplicate sync buys nothing.
rejected: Run your own sync anyway — trust but verify is the safer posture, and an extra sync is cheap.
